title: Security review: Data residency & region pinning
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked CareBridge through region pinning, data residency controls, audit logging, KMS integrations and sub-processor mapping. Customer confirmed EU data residency requirement for PHI-adjacent workloads and asked about cross-border processing, SSO/SAML, RBAC and fallbacks to hosted vs dedicated. Agreed next steps: share SOC2/ISO artifacts, provide EU region test pilot pricing and schedule technical deep dive with platform engineers.
action_items: Ava - Send SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certificates + pen test summary by 2026-12-20
Diego - Draft architecture note on region pinning and fallback behavior and share by 2026-12-22
Jonas - Share sample prompt flow and estimated qps for pilot by 2026-12-21
next_steps: Redwood to share security pack and sub-processor list
Schedule 60min technical deep dive with CareBridge infra (Diego + Jonas) week of 2026-12-27
Provide EU region pilot pricing and capacity options for Dedicated vs Hosted
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-18 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~48m | Attendees: Ava Thompson, Diego Morales - Redwood; Elena Park, Jonas Li, Priya Sharma - CareBridge
[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll kick off. I'm Ava, AE on the account, and Diego's our solutions engineer. Quick agenda — walk through data residency, region pinning, KMS/encryption, audit logs, sub-processors, then Q&A. Elena, you wanna quick context?
[00:22] Elena: Yeah hi, thanks. We need to confirm that any PHI-adjacent processing for EU patients stays in EU, like region pinned. Also interested in cross-border when we do analytics in US, but need legal's take.
[00:45] Ava: Totally, that's what we'll focus on. Diego, do you wanna start with how Redwood handles region pinning?
[01:05] Diego: Sure — high level, we've got routing policies that can pin by customer or project to region-level endpoints. For hosted customers we offer EU-only tenancy option, we can route all inference traffic to eu-west and not replicate to us-east unless you opt in. There's also a Dedicated mode where you reserve capacity in a region.
[01:30] Jonas: When you say "not replicate" — what about logs and telemetry? Does that cross-border?
[01:45] Diego: Good q. By default audit logs and traces live in same region as the pinned deployment for EU-pin customers. We have separate storage buckets per region; cross-region replication is off unless customer enables it. There are a handful of telemetry events that the control plane uses — we can scope those.
[02:12] Elena: How about sub-processors? We use vendors that require us to know if data will move to third countries.
[02:28] Ava: We'll share our current sub-processor list — it's in the security pack — Diego, correct me if that list needs updating?
[02:36] Diego: Yep we'll attach the latest. Note: some GPU hosting partners use global infra for provisioning, but customer data plane is kept region-scoped. I want to call out one nuance — for hosted multi-tenant model catalog updates, model artifacts may be fetched from central storage. For EU-pinned deployments we serve model weights from region caches to avoid cross-border transfer, but earlier infra calls might contact central control plane endpoints for metadata only.
[03:10] Priya: That's fine as long as metadata doesn't contain identifiers.
[03:18] Diego: Agreed — metadata is limited to model id/version and metrics, not prompt content.
[03:30] Elena: KMS question — can we BYOK? We have strict key residency and need customer-managed keys for EU.
[03:44] Diego: Yes, we support KMS integrations. For cloud hosted we integrate with customer AWS KMS / Google Cloud KMS / Azure Key Vault. Keys can be region-scoped and we support Bring Your Own Key for encryption at rest of persisted artifacts (KV cache snapshots, logs). For Dedicated/private deployments you can run HSMs on-prem.
[04:10] Jonas: Is encryption of in-flight traffic TLS only, or do you also support mTLS to internal endpoints?
[04:22] Diego: TLS for public endpoints, and mTLS for private peering or Dedicated connections. We also support customer certificate rotation.
[04:35] Elena: Audit logs — retention policy, access controls, and export? We need 1 year retention by default and ability to export to our SIEM in EU.
[04:50] Ava: We can configure retention; default is 90 days for hosted, but for enterprise customers you can extend retention and we can push logs to customer-managed sinks in the same region. Diego will cover the export mechanics?
[05:05] Diego: Right — we have log-forwarders that can push JSON logs to customer S3 buckets (or GCS) in region, or integrate with SIEMs via syslog/HTTPS. RBAC on logs is enforced via Redwood Console — you can restrict who can request exports.
[05:28] Elena: Who has access to raw prompt/response? We need strict RBAC to prevent support engineers from seeing PHI content.
[05:40] Diego: Good point — console access is role-based. We also provide redaction settings so PII can be redacted before logs persist. For sensitive accounts, support sessions are audited and require owner approval.
[06:05] Priya: On sub-processors again — do you list where model weights are stored (CDN / caches)? We need to include that in DPIA.
[06:18] Ava: We'll include that in the sub-processor mapping doc. We also have a note that model weights for EU-pinned deployments are cached in-region; CDN edge nodes are in the same region when the pin is active.
[06:35] Jonas: How do fallbacks work? If EU capacity exhausted do you fail requests or route to US? We cannot route PHI to US by default.
[06:48] Diego: We have policy controls — can be set to fail closed (reject requests when region saturated) or fail open with anonymization (strip identifiers and route to fallback). For PHI workloads you can set strict fail-over to disabled. We'll include config examples.
[07:12] Elena: Do you have SOC 2 Type II? And ISO?
[07:20] Ava: Yes, SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 — we'll share current certs and the SOC 2 report under NDA.
[07:30] Priya: Pen test? Third-party vulnerability scan?
[07:34] Ava: Annual pentest and quarterly vuln scans; high level summary and remediation timeline included.
[07:46] Jonas: Any paid add-ons for stricter data residency guarantees? Like dedicated control plane or private VPC-only control plane?
[07:58] Diego: For Private deployment we can run the control plane inside customer VPC — that removes cross-border control plane traffic. Dedicated gives you compute in region and network isolation; Private gives you the option to run control plane in your environment.
[08:20] Elena: What about EU data subject requests and deletion? If a patient wants deletion, how do you ensure prompt/resp data is removed?
[08:32] Diego: We have deletion APIs and a purge workflow — for EU-pinned tenants purge jobs run against region-local stores. For backups, we mark and delete during retention windows; for stricter SLAs we can offer expedite deletion as part of enterprise contract.
[08:55] Priya: Need to ensure legal receives the sub-processor list and DPA amendment.
[09:02] Ava: Yes we'll attach the DPA and propose language for EU residency clause.
[09:12] Elena: A couple more technicals — does KV cache ever leave region for warm-up? We use long context and want low latency.
[09:25] Diego: KV cache is managed per-region. For models with shared caching (for efficiency) we do region-level caches; we don't replicate KV cache cross-border. Occasionally control-plane warming jobs fetch model shards, but those are metadata-only or done through region nodes. I will get the exact sequence diagram to you.
[09:50] Jonas: For the pilot we plan ~50 qps, mostly short prompts. What's expected latency in EU hosted?
[10:00] Diego: For small context and typical models, 50 qps in eu-west we've seen median 80-120ms per token for optimized weights on our runtime; we'll run a benchmark during the tech deep dive.
[10:20] Elena: Are there any sub-processors in US that would see logs despite EU pin?
[10:30] Ava: Not by default. Some monitoring/alerting services are US-based; we can provide EU-local alternatives or self-hosted integrations. We'll map them out.
[11:00] Priya: Regarding SSO — we require SAML with enforced SCIM for provisioning and strict session timeout.
[11:12] Diego: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. You can enforce session expiry and MFA via your IdP; Redwood honors those settings.
[11:30] Elena: Do you offer customer-managed RBAC groups mapped to IdP groups?
[11:36] Diego: Yes group mapping is supported; we import IdP groups and map to console roles.
[11:45] Jonas: Any encryption-at-rest specifics for embeddings and model intermediate artifacts?
[11:55] Diego: Encrypted at rest using AES-256, keys managed in customer KMS when BYOK enabled. Snapshots of KV cache and embeddings are encrypted with the same key and stored regionally.
[12:12] Ava: Quick pause — any blockers so far from legal or security?
[12:18] Priya: We need the DPA edits and sub-processor list, plus the SOC2 report under NDA. Also architecture details about control plane endpoints.
[12:30] Ava: Noted. We'll send the docs and schedule the deep dive.
[12:36] Elena: One more question on cross-border analytics — we do de-identified analytics in US. What constitutes de-identified?
[12:48] Diego: We can offer transformation pipelines that strip PII before export. De-identification depends on technique; we usually hash identifiers and remove free-text PHI. For highly regulated data we'd recommend on-prem processing or Dedicated region-only analytics.
[13:20] Jonas: Ok — can you also clarify sub-processor jurisdictions for the ML infra provider (compute)?
[13:30] Ava: Yes we'll include a breakdown: compute partners, storage providers, monitoring vendors and region of operations.
[13:40] Priya: For the DPA we'd like a clause that forbids routing PHI outside EU without explicit approval.
[13:50] Ava: We can propose that language; Diego will draft the technical controls to enforce it.
[14:05] Diego: I'll include policy config examples — how to set fail-closed and pin region in the API and console.
[14:18] Elena: Can Redwood's control plane metadata include hashed user identifiers, or do you send clear IDs?
[14:28] Diego: We can mask or hash identifiers; default is hashed for pinned deployments. We'll document fields that flow to control plane.
[14:45] Jonas: For the upcoming pilot, do we need a long-term contract for Dedicated? Or can we start hosted with EU pin and then convert?
[14:58] Ava: You can start hosted with EU pin and later move to Dedicated. Dedicated requires capacity commitment but we offer migration tooling and can migrate model versions.
[15:12] Elena: Any penalties or downtime during migration?
[15:18] Diego: Usually minimal; we do blue-green migrates per model version and can do canaries. We'll plan a maintenance window if needed.
[15:35] Priya: One last legal ask — indemnity around data breaches?
[15:42] Ava: We'll pass to contracts; standard enterprise addendum with breach notification timelines and liability caps.
[15:52] Elena: Great. Can we get a sample config that shows how to pin org_id to eu-west and failover disabled?
[16:05] Diego: Yes, I'll attach a sample YAML and console screenshots.
[16:18] Jonas: About sub-processors — do you have an escalation path if a sub-processor changes jurisdiction? We need notification within 30 days.
[16:30] Ava: We include notification windows in our DPA; we'll confirm 30 days.
[16:40] Priya: Anything else on compliance — GDPR DPIA sample?
[16:48] Ava: We'll share a DPIA template and example entries for inference workloads.
[17:00] Elena: Ok summarizing — we need SOC2+ISO, sub-processor list with jurisdictions, DPA edits, architecture diagram for control plane and KV flow, sample region-pin config, and a tech deep dive.
[17:18] Ava: Yep — that's our action items. We'll follow up by EOD Monday.
[17:30] Jonas: Thanks all.
[17:38] Meeting end: ~48m.
